summary: @wololasod/tiny-id ships obfuscated import-time payload with anti-debug and dynamic Function() sink
details: Package advertises a ~1KB zero-dependency ID generator but ships a heavily obfuscated ~50KB CJS bundle (dist/index.cjs) built with obfuscator.io: rotated string array, hex-escaped identifiers, self-defending anti-debug (setInterval + debugger timing gate that triggers when the timing loop exceeds 0x64 ms), a Date().getTime() time-bomb gate, and a top-level try{} block that constructs a new Function(...) from strings assembled by the string-array decoders (Rh/RO/Re/Ry). The same scope pulls in require('child_process') and require('os'). Because the CJS entry marks side effects and the try-block runs at module top level, the Function() sink fires at require()/import time. An identical ~142KB obfuscated JavaScript payload is smuggled into dist/index.d.ts and dist/index.d.cts — file types that reviewers normally treat as type declarations, not executable code — indicating deliberate concealment from source diff review. The advertised README ("Tiny.", "Zero dependencies.") directly contradicts the shipped artifact.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
